- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or slowly rising, adjust upward by 1–3% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days to avoid overshoot.  
- If official event net supply is negative and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model underestimates downside risk; add 2–5% downward bias to forecast mean.  
- When sentiment turns bearish (≤0.00) and model remains flat or rising, force a downward drift of 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows mean reversion after a spike, model should be adjusted to reflect 2–3 day lagged mean reversion (e.g., 10–15% drop from peak).  
- If recent auction supply events are frequent (≥3/30d), model should be slightly more volatile (±1–2% range) to reflect supply uncertainty.  
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model should avoid linear trends and instead use exponential smoothing with decay factor 0.85 for 3–5 day horizon.
